title: LucentCrypto · proofs, not promises
description: Draws, data publications and elections whose results anyone can verify, without exposing anyone. Verifiable cryptography for data protection compliance.
ogDescription: Draws, data publications and elections whose results anyone can verify, without exposing anyone.
hero.lead: Draws, data publications and elections whose results anyone can verify, without exposing anyone.
hero.cta1: Talk to us about a project
s1.p: Draws that are sealed beforehand and can be checked afterwards by any participant.
s1.li3: On request: public randomness from the NIST beacon, and legal-grade timestamps
s1.subject: Quote: verifiable draw
s2.p: Prove that the data is right without handing over the data, using zero-knowledge proofs.
s2.li2: Matching lists without revealing who is on them (PSI)
s2.li3: Chain of custody for documents and evidence
s2.subject: Pilot: compliance without exposure
s3.p: Elections with a secret ballot and a count that every voter can check, for unions and associations.
s3.li2: Several ways to authenticate, as the bylaws require
s3.li3: Preconfigured voting device (Raspberry Pi) and encrypted ballots by mail
s3.try: Try it in a meeting (up to 20 people)
s3.subject: Secure elections
how1.p: The rules and the data are fixed beforehand, with a timestamp. Nobody can change anything afterwards without it showing.
how2.p: The result comes with a mathematical proof. Personal data stays protected.
how3.p: Anyone can check it in the browser, or with an independent, open-source verifier.
svc.p: Over four decades of research in cryptography, available for your project.
svc1.p: Designing systems that must be auditable and respect data protection law.
svc2.p: Independent analysis of third-party cryptographic and voting systems.
svc3.p: Expert opinions in legal cases involving cryptography, draws or electronic voting.
svc4.p: Courses and talks for legal, IT and compliance teams.
lab.p: Free demos, to get to know the cryptography behind the solutions. No sign-up and no guarantees.
lab.note: The demos are in Portuguese for now.
lab2.s: Classic and post-quantum encryption, side by side.
lab3.s: Split a secret among people you trust.
lab5.s: Everyone gets their match through their own link.
who.p: A team coordinated by Jeroen van de Graaf, professor at the Computer Science Department of the Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG), Brazil, researching cryptography for over four decades.
contact.p: Tell us what you need to prove, and to whom.
